name: US inflation
summary: US CPI about 4.1% a year in October, rising three months; monthly prices up 0.4%, above forecasts
state: FRED data put annual US CPI inflation at 4.08% in October, rising for a third month and inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band. The BLS report of 10 Nov showed consumer prices up 0.4% on the month against a 0.3% forecast, with core prices up 0.3% for a third straight month (Latin Times). The November CPI report is due in mid-December.
for_you: Higher prices for shelter, food and fuel weigh most on lower-income households and those on fixed incomes. Elevated inflation also keeps US borrowing costs high for mortgages, car loans and credit cards.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.08% y/y within 3.0–4.5% Watch band, rising 3 consecutive months

sources.title: FRED — Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.
